I would like to propose the idea that the Dark One and the Creator are one in the same and that honestly the Dark One does not really want to win to break the wheel and end all things.  
 
1.  The Wheel of Time has turned many times and ages repeat themselves. Mortals eventually forget everything about an age when that age comes again. But the Dark One is not a mortal and has seen every age more than once.  Now the same age is never a carbon copy but for the most part it is identical with small variances. With this said it would stand a reason that the Dark One knows how an Age plays out after seeing it multiple times and would know how to stop any part that would stop him...but he doesn’t.
2.  We are told multiple times that if the seals on the Dark Ones prison is broken he would enter the world and mankind would lose. If this is true then the Dark One chooses not to enter the world and do this or this is a misconception. I say this because when Lanfear created the first hole in the Age of Legends years passed by before all our war struck and the first Myrdraal and Trollocs were created. If the first holds true then the Dark One had ample opportunity. He had ripe world that knew only peace (not ready for war) and could have moved right on in. Instead he took his time polluting the minds of men and set himself up to topple the Utopia and restore the world to a new equilibrium. In essence the world had drifted too far toward good and needed a reset button. 
3.  The whole series is about balance. Saidin and Saidar, Aes Sendai and Asha’man, Men and Women, Light vs Dark. It would stand to reason that the Creator and the Dark One are either the same or just two sides of the same coin forever pushing and pulling on each other to do nothing more than establish the necessary equilibrium for the world. 
4.  Ishamael, whether mad or not, has stated that the Dragon Reborn has fought the Dark One every Age for all eternity and that at some points has even sided with the Shadow.  If true that leads me to believe that in some ages the Dark One does win but the end result would only be a shift in the balance which at a later date when gone too far is once again reset which the Dark One would allow to happen.  
Let me know your thoughts 

Hello Demiar,
It would seem that your logic is the same as Herid Fel in Lord of Chaos, Chapter 18, A Taste of Solitude. He tried to comfort Rand with the notion that the Dark One could not win because he had never won. The Wheel of Time will re-turn to the Battle and the Dragon Reborn will win, as he always has. Rand responded: "Unless the Dark One breaks free...to break the Wheel of Time and remake Time and the World in his own image!" When I read this, it was a major mind blowing and illuminating concept. I had been believing the same as Herid Fel (may the Light bless his memory); that is: Rand had to win. The fact that he could lose was the mountain that he had to carry.
I think that the Dark One is a creature of the Creator. He created him for balance, yes. Without Darkness there is no struggle for Light. Without struggle there is no winning. No proving that within his creatures is a goodness so great that they would die to allow others they love to live. This is what defeats the Dark One. All of the Dark One's followers are led by his Darkness, selfishness. When the Wheel turns, selflessness wins over selfishness every time.
The fact is that the Dark One knows that selflessness will stop him and so does everthing he can think of to counteract it, but has not won. SO FAR! The taint was a good, scratch that, completely evil idea. I think that this was a new idea of the Dark One this time around, shall we say. One of those 'small variances'. It could have worked if not for Rand and Nynaeve.
Let us hope that in the Age to come the Dark One does not think of a way to win. He has never won or the Wheel of Time would have been destroyed and with it the fabric of time that is woven with life. 

If or when this happens, we will see a big empty space on our bookshelves!!!
